purpose: Authoritative inventory/disposition map for normalizing the Havenwild native editor and F3 developer authoring experience before behavioral rewrites.

dispositions.KEEP: Canonical behavior/owner. Preserve and integrate with minimal structural change.
dispositions.MERGE: Functionality is useful but must be folded into the named canonical owner; old module can disappear after migration.
dispositions.ADAPT: Module remains but its API/state/UI must conform to Authoring V2.
dispositions.DEPRECATE: Keep for compatibility/regression only; do not add features. Replace then remove.
dispositions.DELETE_LATER: No active authority; remove after verifying unique behavior/data has been salvaged.

nonGoals: No runtime behavior changes in this pass.
No asset, terrain, worldgen, save, or renderer authority reset.
No module deletion in this pass.
lockedDecisions: The existing GREEN runtime remains the regression reference.
LDtk/GameMaker-style direct world construction is permanent functionality.
Native editor, F3 runtime edit mode, PIE and automation must use the same authoring commands and asset identities.
F3 Developer Overlay is lightweight inspection/diagnostics by default; Runtime Edit is explicitly entered.
Source sheets are containers; normal asset palettes show semantic/runtime assets rather than whole sheets.
Manual exact tile placement/rotation/mirroring where legal remains available even when autotiling exists.
Manual authored structures/patterns can be promoted into PCG exemplars.
Spawn placement is a first-class Game Canvas tool.

findings.title: Authoring identity is still legacy-first
findings.finding: AuthoringSession and DocumentAuthority are promising V2 adapters, but EditorApp still stores legacy viewport/tool/layer/document state directly. V2 currently snapshots legacy state instead of owning it.
findings.decision: Promote AuthoringSession + DocumentAuthority to the authoritative context spine in Pass 2.

findings.title: Duplicate scene/world tool and layer models
findings.finding: SceneEditTool and WorldEditTool duplicate the same verbs, while SceneLayerMode/WorldLayerMode compete with CanvasLayerKind.
findings.decision: One UniversalTool + scope-aware target + CanvasLayerKind. Scene/World become edit scopes, not independent tool systems.

findings.title: Layer classification still contains filename/string heuristics
findings.finding: Stamp layer selection searches names/categories for water, pond, path, cliff, building, house, roof, wall and similar strings.
findings.decision: Asset Catalog V2 must declare typed semantic layer/category. Filename guessing becomes validation fallback only and cannot be runtime/editor authority.

findings.title: Asset source sheets and usable assets remain conflated
findings.finding: The project has source-sheet inventory and bounded thumbnail infrastructure, but normal selection still exposes source/donor records and promotion candidates alongside usable assets.
findings.decision: Assets Studio V2 owns Source Sheets, Semantic Assets, Runtime Assets and Review separately; normal palettes expose semantic/runtime assets only.

findings.title: F3 is not lightweight
findings.finding: Pressing F3 currently sets both dev_mode and build_mode and expands the editor, despite the status text calling it lightweight.
findings.decision: F3 toggles Developer Overlay only. Runtime Edit is a separate explicit action/mode.

findings.title: Runtime dev tools duplicate native authoring authority
findings.finding: Runtime has its own tabs, brush modes, object editor, map editor and paint editor.
findings.decision: Runtime developer mode becomes a frontend over haven_authoring commands and shared metadata; it does not own a second editor model.

findings.title: Spawn authoring is not a first-class shared workflow
findings.finding: A selected-cell player spawn hotkey exists and authoring capabilities include NPC/debug spawn, but there is no unified Spawn tool/palette/typed anchor model across native editor and F3.
findings.decision: Add typed spawn/anchor definitions: Player Start, Play From Here, NPC, NPC/animal/resource spawner, encounter, transition destination and PCG anchor.

findings.title: EditorApp remains a broad state container
findings.finding: EditorApp directly owns world/scene selection, multiple palettes, asset intake, specialized studios, several canvas states, legacy tools/layers, documents, diagnostics and runtime launch state.
findings.decision: Pass 2 introduces owned sub-state services (session/documents/game-canvas/assets/runtime bridge) and migrates fields incrementally without a big-bang rewrite.

findings.title: Detached editor remnants remain in source tree
findings.finding: These files exist but are not declared by the active app module tree. Some contain reusable concepts; others are superseded.
findings.decision: Salvage bridge/region behavior into active owners, then delete remnants. GUI Studio can be removed after verifying no unique behavior is missing from Game Canvas UI.

findings.title: Manual world construction must be permanent, not a fallback
findings.finding: Direct visual editing and PCG exemplar infrastructure exist, but they are not yet the primary, coherent LDtk-style workflow.
findings.decision: Game Canvas V2 permanently supports semantic paint + exact raw tile/region placement + manual overrides + save-as-pattern/prefab.
